findings.detail: snapshot() accepts in-root symlinks by following them, but materialize() recreates every input as a regular file. For example, declare subject.txt and alias.txt, where alias.txt links to subject.txt, and have the check read alias.txt. A patch changing subject.txt no longer reaches that check in the private copy. An assertion plant incorrectly fails, or a declared control incorrectly publishes control-green despite behavior that would differ in the original tree.
findings.fix: Preserve and fingerprint symlink relationships, requiring their targets among declared inputs, and add a regression that patches a target read through its symlink. Alternatively, explicitly reject symlinked inputs before execution.
findings.title: Uncited: Materialization silently breaks accepted symlink relationships.

strengths: Rendering independently validates step evidence and current input fingerprints.
Regression coverage challenges assertion, restoration, timeout and publication guards.
summary: Reviewed all 32 membership paths and the committed changes against the supplied historical guidelines. One Important defect remains in private-copy semantics. Review was static and read-only; tests were not run, and GitHub metadata verification was unavailable.
